source_meta._title: Player can retain Soul Speed effect by bridging

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 5 in a singleplayer world. Use Creative mode with cheats during construction and item setup, then Survival mode for the trigger sequence. No particular seed, dimension, biome, or coordinates are specified.
preconditions: Launch Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 5, not the fixed version 24w18a or any later version.
Use Soul Soil for the first bridge extension. Do not substitute Soul Sand; the report states that Soul Sand lowers the player too far for this procedure to work properly.
Use a full, non-Soul-Speed block for the following extension. This plan uses Stone as the unspecified normal block.
Keep the Soul Soil in hotbar slot 1 and Stone in hotbar slot 2 so the block type can be changed without interrupting movement.

During the trigger sequence, keep the Sneak action continuously active, use only forward movement, and do not step or move backward. With default controls, Sneak is Left Shift, forward is W, and backward is S.
If Left Shift is released, S is pressed, the player steps backward, or the player falls before reaching the trigger, restart the movement sequence from the original platform edge.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation for Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 5 and launch it. At the title screen, confirm that the displayed version is exactly 1.16 Pre-release 5.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen displays Java Edition 1.16 Pre-release 5.

steps.action: Create a new singleplayer world in Creative mode. Leave cheats enabled so the report-supplied item command and the later game-mode command can be executed.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered a Creative-mode singleplayer world and can use commands.

steps.action: Wait until the surrounding terrain has rendered and player movement, inventory interaction, and chat commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are rendered and the player responds immediately to movement input.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the report-supplied command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A pair of Netherite Boots is added to the player's inventory and the command does not display a syntax error.

steps.action: Press E to open the inventory. Locate the Netherite Boots created by the command, verify that their tooltip lists Soul Speed III, and move them into the feet armor slot. Close the inventory with E.
steps.success_cue: The Soul Speed III Netherite Boots are visibly equipped in the feet armor slot.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with E. Use the Search Items tab to find Soul Soil, then place a stack of Soul Soil into hotbar slot 1.
steps.success_cue: Soul Soil occupies hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory remains open, search for Stone and place a stack of Stone into hotbar slot 2. Close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: Soul Soil is in hotbar slot 1 and Stone is in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: In a clear area, construct a small Stone starting platform whose top surface is at least four blocks above the ground. Make the platform at least 3 blocks by 3 blocks, and choose one edge with at least six blocks of unobstructed horizontal air beyond it. The block at the chosen starting edge must be Stone, not Soul Soil or Soul Sand.
steps.success_cue: A stable elevated Stone platform exists with a straight, unobstructed bridging direction extending over open air.

steps.action: Land on the platform and stop Creative flight. Stand several blocks back from the selected edge, facing directly toward the open-air bridging direction.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on the platform, is not flying, and is facing the selected edge head-on.

steps.action: Press T, enter the game-mode command including the leading slash, and press Enter to conduct the movement sequence in Survival mode.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms the game mode was changed to Survival, and the player is standing normally on the platform.

steps.action: Press 1 to select the Soul Soil in hotbar slot 1. Keep the camera facing straight toward the selected platform edge.
steps.success_cue: Soul Soil is shown as the selected item in the player's hand.

steps.action: Press and continuously hold the Sneak action, default Left Shift. While continuing to hold Sneak, press and hold forward, default W, until ledge protection stops the player at the platform edge. Do not press backward, default S.
steps.success_cue: The player is crouched at the outer edge, still facing forward over open air, without falling or moving backward.

steps.action: Without releasing Sneak or forward movement, angle the camera downward until the crosshair targets the outward vertical face near the top of the Stone block supporting the player. Right-click once to attach one Soul Soil block to that face, extending the platform horizontally at the same height.
steps.success_cue: One Soul Soil block is attached directly beyond the Stone edge, with its top surface level with the platform.

steps.action: Continue holding Sneak and forward movement so the player advances from the Stone platform onto the newly placed Soul Soil. Keep facing the same direction and do not step backward.
steps.success_cue: The crouched player is positioned on the Soul Soil extension and has not reversed direction or released Sneak.

steps.action: Without releasing Sneak or forward movement, press 2 to change the selected hotbar item from Soul Soil to Stone. Continue applying forward input toward the open edge.
steps.exact_input: 2 while continuing to hold Left Shift + W
steps.success_cue: Stone is selected while the player remains crouched on the Soul Soil and continues pressing toward the outer edge.

steps.action: At the outer edge of the Soul Soil, keep Sneak and forward movement held. Aim down at the outward vertical face of the Soul Soil block and right-click once to attach a Stone block at the same height directly ahead.
steps.exact_input: Right-click while continuing to hold Left Shift + W
steps.success_cue: A Stone block is attached directly beyond the Soul Soil, forming a straight Stone–Soul Soil–Stone path.

steps.action: Continue holding Sneak and forward movement until the player advances from the Soul Soil onto the newly placed Stone. Do not release Sneak, stop to reposition, or use backward movement before this transition is complete.
steps.success_cue: The player has just crossed onto the Stone extension while continuously sneaking and moving in the original forward direction, with no backward movement since entering the Soul Soil.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just moved directly from the Soul Soil extension onto the first Stone extension while continuously holding Sneak and forward movement, and no backward movement has occurred. Hand control to the observation subsystem immediately without changing direction, releasing Sneak, or walking back.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, coordinates, dimension, game mode, platform design, or which non-Soul-Speed block to use. An elevated Stone platform, Creative-mode construction, and Survival-mode execution are practical choices rather than stated requirements.

The Soul Speed boots command is copied exactly from a report comment that explicitly presents it for 21w06a. Its exact execution was not definitively verified from an allowed primary web source for the recommended version, 1.16 Pre-release 5. If that exact command produces a syntax error, do not silently modernize or alter its NBT; record the setup as blocked by version-specific command uncertainty.

The report also describes a separate inverse sequence in which the first extension is a normal block and subsequent extensions are Soul Speed blocks. This plan targets the issue title's primary Soul-Soil-then-normal-block sequence so that there is one unambiguous trigger step and immediate observation handoff.

source_meta._title: All arrow types lose their name/NBT data when shot and picked up

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.2 in a new single-player world using the integrated server. Begin in Creative mode with cheats enabled so the bow, arrows, and anvil can be obtained deterministically and the arrows can be renamed without acquiring experience levels. Change to Survival mode before firing so the bow uses an arrow from the custom-named stack. Use default controls unless the corresponding actions have been rebound.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.2, the first version listed as affected; do not use fix version 23w43a.
Create a new single-player world with Game Mode set to Creative and Allow Cheats enabled.
Use an unmodified client without gameplay-changing mods or datapacks.
Keep at least one empty inventory slot available for the recovered arrow.
Use a plain, unenchanted bow; in particular, do not use an Infinity-enchanted bow.
Prepare a clear patch of solid ground where an arrow can be fired into a block a few blocks away and recovered without falling into water, fire, lava, a void, or an inaccessible gap.
Do not carry any ordinary, unnamed arrows other than the stack that will be renamed; this prevents an unnamed recovered arrow from merging into an unrelated stack.

steps.action: From the title screen, select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, enable Allow Cheats under the additional world options, and create the world. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a loaded single-player world, can fly, has no health or hunger bars, and can use commands.

steps.action: Locate a clear area with solid ground. If necessary, fly a short distance from trees, water, lava, cliffs, or other obstacles, then land.
steps.success_cue: There is a visible solid ground surface at least several blocks long, with enough room to shoot and walk to an embedded arrow.

steps.action: Press the inventory action key, default E, to open the Creative inventory.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open and item categories or the item search interface are visible.

steps.action: Find the Bow item in the Creative inventory and place one plain bow into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine slots at the bottom of the inventory.
steps.success_cue: A plain bow is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Find the Arrow item and place one stack of regular arrows into a separate inventory or hotbar slot. Do not obtain any additional unnamed arrow stacks.
steps.success_cue: One stack of regular arrows is present and no other arrow stacks are in the inventory.

steps.action: Find the Anvil item and place one anvil into another hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: An anvil item is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Select the hotbar slot containing the anvil by pressing its corresponding number key, aim at the top of a solid ground block, and right-click to place it. Minecraft 1.4.2 added anvils and supports renaming items with them. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/1.4.2_%28Java_Edition%29?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: A placed anvil block is visible directly in front of the player.

steps.action: Aim at the placed anvil and right-click it to open the anvil interface.
steps.success_cue: The anvil interface is open, showing a left input slot, a right input slot, a name field, and an output slot.

steps.action: Move the entire regular-arrow stack into the anvil's left input slot. Click the name field, remove the existing item name if one is displayed, and type the custom name exactly as supplied by the report.
steps.success_cue: The name field contains exactly MC-1981 and a renamed arrow stack is available in the output slot.

steps.action: Click the output slot to take the renamed arrow stack and place it in an inventory or hotbar slot. Leave the right anvil input slot empty. In Creative mode, the anvil operation is not blocked by the normal experience-level limit. ([ru.minecraft.wiki](https://ru.minecraft.wiki/w/1.4.2_%28Java_Edition%29?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Hovering over the arrow stack in the inventory displays the custom item name MC-1981.

steps.action: Close the anvil interface with E. Ensure that the plain bow and the MC-1981 arrow stack remain in the inventory and that at least one other inventory slot is empty.
steps.success_cue: Normal world view is visible; the bow and custom-named arrows remain available, and an empty inventory slot exists.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the historical game-mode command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter. Numeric game-mode arguments and mode-first command ordering were supported by the command implementation used in this period. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki%3AIssues/Weekly_12w37a?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: Chat reports a successful game-mode change, and the Survival health, hunger, and armor interface appears above the hotbar.

steps.action: Press E and re-check the arrow stack before shooting. Hover over it and confirm that it is still named MC-1981, then close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The pre-shot arrow stack still displays MC-1981, and the game has returned to normal first-person view in Survival mode.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the plain bow by pressing the corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel. Confirm that the renamed arrow stack remains elsewhere in the inventory as ammunition.
steps.success_cue: The bow is visible in the player's hand, and the MC-1981 arrow stack is present in the inventory.

steps.action: Stand approximately 3 to 6 blocks from a clear patch of solid ground. Aim downward at a ground block far enough ahead that the fired arrow can visibly embed in the block instead of striking the player or traveling out of sight.
steps.success_cue: The crosshair points at an unobstructed solid ground block a few blocks in front of the player.

steps.action: Hold right-click, the default Use Item control, until the bow is fully drawn.
steps.success_cue: The bow model is visibly pulled back to its fully drawn state while the crosshair remains aimed at the target ground block.

steps.action: Release right-click once to fire exactly one arrow into the targeted ground block. Do not fire additional arrows.
steps.success_cue: One arrow is visibly embedded in the ground, and the custom-named arrow stack's count has decreased by one.

steps.action: Wait until the fired arrow is stationary and remains embedded in the ground. Do not open the inventory or inspect item data yet.
steps.success_cue: The arrow has stopped moving and is reachable by walking over it.

steps.action: Walk directly over the embedded arrow using the movement controls, normally W, until it is collected. Stop moving immediately after the arrow disappears from the ground.
steps.success_cue: The arrow entity disappears from the ground and the pickup sound plays or an arrow item is added to the inventory; the recovered item's name has not yet been evaluated.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has just walked over and collected the single arrow that was fired from the MC-1981 custom-named arrow stack. Stop further input and hand control to the observation subsystem for inventory and item-data inspection.
uncertainties: The report supplies `/give @s minecraft:arrow{display:{Name:'{"text":"MC-1981"}'}}`, but that exact command is not executable in the recommended Minecraft 1.4.2 environment. Custom item NBT support for `/give` was added in the 1.7.2 development cycle, after 1.4.2. The plan therefore preserves the required custom name by using the 1.4.2 anvil-renaming mechanic rather than silently rewriting the command into unsupported historical syntax. ([zh.minecraft.wiki](https://zh.minecraft.wiki/w/Java%E7%89%881.7.2?utm_source=openai))

The report does not prescribe a game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, or server type. A single-player Creative setup followed by Survival-mode firing is a practical deterministic choice, not a stated requirement of the report.

The issue title refers to all arrow types, but the supplied reproduction procedure specifically creates and fires a regular arrow. Minecraft 1.4.2 predates later tipped and spectral arrow variants, so this plan reproduces the report's regular-arrow case only.

The exact layout of the 1.4.2 Creative inventory depends on the selected item category. The executor may obtain Bow, Arrow, and Anvil through the available category tabs if a search field is not exposed in the current tab.

source_meta._title: Horse armor loses its NBT data when equipped on horses via right-clicking

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3 in a vanilla single-player world. Use Survival mode with commands available through cheats. No particular seed or dimension is specified; perform the reproduction in the Overworld in an open area where a horse can be approached directly.
preconditions: Launch exactly Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3, the first version listed as affected in the report; do not use the fixed version 1.20 Pre-release 2.
Create or load a single-player world with cheats enabled so that the supplied /summon and /give commands can be executed from in-game chat.
Use Survival mode as a minimally interfering implementation choice; the report does not specify a required game mode.
Ensure the player has at least one empty inventory slot to receive the leather horse armor.
Stand on solid ground in an open area with enough room for a horse to appear at the player's current X, Y, Z coordinates.
Use the configured Use Item/Place Block control when instructed to right-click; its default input is the right mouse button.

steps.action: Launch the Minecraft Launcher, select or create an installation that runs Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.3, start the game, and enter the cheats-enabled test world.
steps.success_cue: The player is controlling a character in a loaded 1.19.3 world, surrounding chunks are rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: If the player is not already in Survival mode, open chat and switch to Survival mode. Include the leading slash because this is an in-game chat command.
steps.success_cue: The player is in Survival mode, indicated by the normal health and hunger bars above the hotbar.

steps.action: Move to an open location, stop moving, and make sure the block occupied by the player and the nearby blocks are clear enough for a horse to spawn without being trapped inside other blocks.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on solid ground with a clear, directly reachable space at the player's current position.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's horse summon command exactly as supplied—including the leading slash, capitalization, coordinates, and NBT—and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: A horse appears at or immediately beside the player's position. It remains stationary because NoAI is enabled and is already tamed because Tame is enabled.

steps.action: Step back far enough to see the summoned horse clearly while remaining within normal right-click interaction range. Do not mount or open the horse inventory.
steps.success_cue: The stationary horse is visible under the crosshair and can be reached with a normal right-click.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the report's item-give command exactly as supplied—including the leading slash and all NBT punctuation and quoting—and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: One leather horse armor item is added to the player's inventory; it has the custom display name MC-258360 and a custom dyed color.

steps.action: Place the supplied leather horse armor in the hotbar if necessary, then select its hotbar slot. To move it when it is not already in the hotbar, press E to open the inventory, drag the armor into one of the nine bottom hotbar slots, close the inventory with E, and select that slot using the corresponding number key or mouse wheel.
steps.exact_input: E, then hotbar slot key 1-9 as applicable
steps.success_cue: The leather horse armor is visible in the player's main hand, and its hotbar slot is highlighted as the active slot.

steps.action: While standing beside the horse and holding the custom leather horse armor in the active hand, center the crosshair on the horse's body and use the Use Item/Place Block control once—right mouse button by default. Do not open the horse inventory before performing this quick-equip interaction.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once on the horse while holding the custom leather horse armor
steps.success_cue: The right-click interaction has completed and the horse is now visibly wearing leather horse armor; no inventory-based equipping method was used.

stor.handoff_condition: The custom-NBT leather horse armor has just been equipped directly by right-clicking the tamed horse, and the horse is visibly wearing it. Hand control to the observation subsystem before performing any further interaction, removal, replacement, or inventory-based equipping.
uncertainties: The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated server. A cheats-enabled single-player world is selected because both supplied commands and the right-click interaction can be executed there without changing the stated reproduction path.

The report does not specify a game mode. Survival mode is selected to make transfer of the armor from the player's hand to the horse unambiguous and to avoid possible Creative-mode item-retention differences.
No world seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, or graphics settings are specified; none are added as reproduction requirements.
The report states that the issue does not occur when using the horse inventory, so the horse inventory must not be used to equip the armor before the trigger step.

source_meta._title: Firework Star item displays have inconsistent color updates

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.5 Pre-Release 3 in a single-player test world. Use Creative mode, or another game mode with cheats enabled, so the player can execute /summon and /data commands. No particular world seed is required.
preconditions: Configure and launch Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.5 Pre-Release 3, the first version listed as affected. Do not use the fix version, 1.20.5 Release Candidate 2.
Use a disposable single-player world in which the player has permission to execute commands. Creating the world in Creative mode is a practical way to ensure command access.
Use a fresh area with no pre-existing item display entities nearby. This prevents the nearest-entity selector in the modification command from targeting an unrelated display.
Stand in an open, fully loaded location where an item rendered at the player's position can be viewed. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
Remain at approximately the same position while running the two summon commands so both item displays are created together as specified by the report.

steps.action: Launch a Minecraft Java Edition game installation configured for the recommended affected version. At the main menu, verify that the displayed game version is 1.20.5 Pre-Release 3.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and identifies the running version as 1.20.5 Pre-Release 3.

steps.action: Open a disposable single-player world with command permission. If creating a new world, select Creative mode and create the world; no specific seed is required.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> Game Mode: Creative -> Create New World
steps.success_cue: The player is inside the test world and can open chat and execute commands.

steps.action: Move to a clear location with no unrelated item display entities nearby. Stop moving and wait until surrounding chunks are rendered and player controls respond normally. Keep this location for both summon commands.
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in a fully loaded area, with no unrelated item displays close enough to interfere with the nearest-entity selector.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the first summon command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a syntax or permission error, and a firework-star item display exists at the player's position.

steps.action: Without changing the player's position, press T again, enter the same summon command a second time exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The two entities occupy the same location and may visually overlap.
steps.success_cue: The second summon command completes without an error. Two item display entities have now been summoned at the player's location, even if their overlapping rendered items appear as a single firework star.

steps.action: Stay near the two summoned displays. Press T to open chat, enter the supplied data modification command exactly, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The selector uses limit=1, so only one of the nearest item displays is selected for modification.
steps.success_cue: The command completes without a syntax, permission, or no-entity-found error, confirming that one nearby item display's firework explosion colors data was modified.

steps.action: Wait briefly after command execution until the game is responsive and the item displays have rendered. Do not issue another command or alter either display.
steps.success_cue: The world is responsive, and the display location remains loaded and visible before leaving the world.

steps.action: Open the pause menu and leave the world using Save and Quit to Title. Wait until the main title screen has fully appeared.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The single-player world has closed and the Minecraft title screen is visible.

steps.action: Rejoin the exact same test world: open the Singleplayer world list, select the world used in the preceding steps, and activate Play Selected World or double-click the world entry. Do not create a new world.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> select the same test world -> Play Selected World
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins loading the same saved world containing the two item displays and the modified entity data.

steps.action: Wait for rejoining to finish. Do not continue until surrounding chunks have rendered, player movement responds normally, and the location where the two item displays were summoned is in view. The player should return near that location because the world was saved while standing beside the displays.
steps.success_cue: The same test world is fully loaded, controls are responsive, and the two co-located item displays are present at the previously used location and ready for observation.

stor.handoff_condition: The player has rejoined the same saved world after modifying one of the two co-located item displays. World loading is complete, controls are responsive, and the item display location is currently in view. Hand control to the observation subsystem before performing any further commands or entity modifications.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a game mode or world seed. Creative mode and an arbitrary disposable world are selected only to provide reliable command permission and do not replace any stated report requirement.

The formal Steps to Reproduce use initial color value -1 and modified value -65536. Comment 3 provides an alternative reproduction using initial value 0 and modified value 16777215. This plan preserves and prioritizes the commands from the formal Steps to Reproduce.

Both summon commands use the same relative coordinates and therefore create overlapping item displays. The report does not require separating them, so the plan preserves their shared position even though visual overlap can make manual entity counting difficult.

The selector in the modification command does not deterministically distinguish between the two displays when both occupy the same coordinates. It is sufficient that limit=1 selects exactly one of them, as required by the report.

The report describes the visual update as inconsistent, so a single execution may not present the same visual state on every run. The plan performs one modification and one reload rather than repeatedly triggering the issue.

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.4.5 in a single-player world using the integrated server. Perform the anvil operations in Survival mode. Enable cheats only to provision a historically valid very damaged anvil, expendable items, and experience levels without introducing crafting or exploration randomness. Use keyboard and mouse controls; instructions name the default controls.
preconditions: Launch the exact full release labeled Minecraft 1.4.5, not the similarly named pre-release and not the fixed version 21w18a or any later version.
Use a new or disposable world so that testing in an old Minecraft version cannot damage a valuable world.
The world must be in Survival mode when the anvil is used and the output is collected.
Cheats must be enabled so the version-compatible setup commands can be entered in single-player chat.
Keep at least three inventory slots free: one for very damaged anvils, one for unnamed cobblestone, and one for renamed output.
Conduct the test on a solid, level surface away from lava, fire, cacti, explosions, the Void, steep drops, and other players or entities that could move or collect an item.
Use a normal left-click on the anvil output. Shift-clicking the output is specifically excluded by the report.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft launcher, select the installation for the full Java Edition release Minecraft 1.4.5, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and displays version 1.4.5.

steps.action: From the title screen, choose Singleplayer, select Create New World, set Game Mode to Survival, open More World Options, set Allow Cheats to ON, and create the world. Do not select Hardcore or Creative as the gameplay mode.
steps.success_cue: A new world begins loading with Survival selected and commands permitted.

steps.action: Wait until the world and nearby chunks finish loading. Do not begin setup while terrain is still appearing or movement is unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: Nearby terrain is rendered, movement responds normally, and the Survival HUD shows hearts and hunger icons.

steps.action: Move to a solid, level area with no nearby environmental hazards. Ensure there is a floor block with open space directly above it where the anvil can be placed.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing next to a safe floor location, and there is no lava, fire, cactus, void edge, or steep drop nearby.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, type the historical 1.4.5 give command exactly as shown, and press Enter. The numeric item ID 145 is an anvil, and item data value 2 selects its most damaged obtainable inventory variant.
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains a stack of anvils using the most visibly cracked damage variant, historically represented by anvil item data value 2.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command, and press Enter to obtain expendable items for repeated low-cost rename operations.
steps.success_cue: A stack of 64 Cobblestone is present in the inventory.

steps.action: Press T, enter the following command, and press Enter. In this version, the uppercase L suffix grants experience levels rather than raw experience points.
steps.success_cue: The experience-level number above the hotbar has increased by 64 levels.

steps.action: Press E to open the player inventory. Identify the hotbar as the row of nine slots at the bottom. If necessary, left-click the very damaged anvil stack and then left-click a hotbar slot to place it there. Put the Cobblestone stack in another accessible inventory or hotbar slot. Press E again to close the inventory.
steps.success_cue: The player inventory is closed, a very damaged anvil is accessible from the hotbar, and the Cobblestone stack is available in the inventory.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the very damaged anvils by pressing its number key or scrolling the mouse wheel until that slot is outlined.
steps.success_cue: A very damaged anvil is shown in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is selected.

steps.action: Aim at the top face of the prepared solid floor block and right-click once to place one very damaged anvil. Do not place it on a gravity-affected or hazardous setup where it could fall before use.
steps.success_cue: One heavily cracked anvil block stands on the floor in front of the player.

steps.action: With an empty cursor and while standing within interaction range, aim at the placed anvil and right-click it once.
steps.success_cue: The anvil interface is open, showing two input slots, an output slot, the item-name field, and the player's inventory.

steps.action: Place exactly one unnamed Cobblestone into the left input slot: left-click the Cobblestone stack to pick it up, right-click the empty left input slot once to deposit one block, and left-click the original inventory slot to return the remainder of the stack. Leave the second input slot empty.
steps.success_cue: The left input contains exactly one Cobblestone, the second input is empty, the remaining unnamed Cobblestone is back in the inventory, and no item remains attached to the mouse cursor.

steps.action: Click the item-name text field in the anvil interface. Press Ctrl+A to select its current text, then type the single lowercase letter shown. This creates a simple rename-only operation.
steps.success_cue: The name field displays "a" and a renamed Cobblestone appears in the output slot.

steps.action: Wait until the output slot is visibly populated and the displayed level cost is affordable. Keep the mouse cursor empty before taking the output.
steps.success_cue: The renamed Cobblestone is available in the output slot, the cost is displayed, and the player has enough experience levels to complete the operation.

steps.action: Move the pointer over the anvil output slot and perform one normal left-click. Do not hold Shift and do not shift-click. This click attempts to pick the completed item up onto the mouse cursor and is the report's trigger action when it coincides with the anvil's final use.
steps.success_cue: On a non-final use, the anvil interface remains open and the renamed Cobblestone is attached to the cursor. On the final use, the anvil block disappears and the interface closes automatically; if that second condition occurs, stop all input immediately and hand off to observation.

steps.action: Only if the interface remained open after step 15, left-click an empty player-inventory slot or the existing stack of identically renamed Cobblestone to put down the cursor-held output. Then repeat steps 12 through 15 with another single unnamed Cobblestone. Continue until an execution of step 15 makes the very damaged anvil disappear and force-closes the interface. Do not manually close the interface during an iteration, and stop immediately when the automatic closure occurs.
steps.success_cue: After each non-breaking iteration, the cursor is empty and the interface is ready for another operation. The loop terminates only when the anvil disappears and the interface closes automatically immediately after the normal output click.

stor.handoff_condition: The final normal left-click on the populated anvil output slot has just caused the very damaged anvil to disappear and the anvil interface to close automatically. The player has not clicked again, moved, opened an inventory, or attempted to collect or relocate any item since that automatic closure. Begin observation now.
uncertainties: The report describes using all of an anvil's "charges," but anvil damage and final breakage are probabilistic rather than a predictable fixed-use counter. Historical mechanic documentation indicates a 12% damage-or-break chance per completed use, so the exact iteration that becomes the trigger cannot be predetermined.

Starting with item data value 2 accelerates setup by placing the anvil directly in its most damaged obtainable state. The report comments support beginning with a damaged anvil, but the report does not provide this exact historical command.

A stack of 64 Cobblestone permits up to 64 rename attempts. There is a very small possibility that the anvil will not break during those attempts; if that occurs, obtain another stack using the same /give command and continue with the same still-placed very damaged anvil.

The report does not specify single-player versus dedicated server, a world seed, coordinates, difficulty, or a particular item operation. Single-player, a safe arbitrary location, and renaming individual Cobblestone blocks were selected as minimal practical implementation choices that preserve the required Survival-mode output-click trigger.

Historical English naming for the item data value 2 anvil variant may appear as "Very Damaged Anvil" rather than the later name "Damaged Anvil." Identify it by data value 2 and by its most heavily cracked appearance.
